Subject: Priya Shah — rapid clarity sprint & evidence log

Team — quick one: hiring manager wants a final recommendation today and we need tight evidence to support a hire/no-hire. Please do two things by EOD PDT: 

1) Fill the attached scorecard (priya_scorecard_template.xlsx) with numeric scores (1-5) and 1–3 bullet evidence points per rubric area (Product sense, System design, Code craft, Communication, Ownership)
2) Drop any short quotes or signal lines into the Notion page (link below) — put evidentiary lines, not summaries.

A couple of alignment anchors to use when writing evidence (short):
- Product sense: candidate showed clear trade-off thinking (give the quote or paraphrase).
- System design: note a specific topology/constraint they proposed, or where they missed a critical constraint.
- Code craft: point to an algorithmic choice or complexity discussion.

If you think we need a 15–20m sync, say so in your reply; otherwise I will aggregate and propose a vote + tiebreak by 5pm.

Attachment: priya_scorecard_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Recruiting Partner — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:03:15 -0700

Thanks Grace — attaching my filled card and a quick 3-line evidence extract (jonas_priya_quicknotes.pdf). Short notes below so it's searchable: 

Scores (prelim): Product 4, System 3, Code 4, Comm 5, Ownership 4.

Evidence bullets (pasteable):
- Product: Asked about metric trade-offs for latency vs consistency; proposed A/B with progressive rollout and rollback hooks.
- System: Proposed event-driven ingestion with per-tenant sharding but missed cache-coherency discussion for cross-tenant reads (important for our use-case).
- Code: Chose a bounded-priority queue approach to backpressure; explained complexity O(n log k) and memory constraints.

Quick vote lean: Yes, with a note on system design gap. Happy to join a 15m if needed.

Attachment: jonas_priya_quicknotes.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:46:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Priya Shah — rapid clarity sprint & evidence log

Adding my card and a slightly longer note (attached: marissa_priya_deepnotes.txt). TL;DR: I lean yes but want a short alignment on system design severity vs compensating strengths. Key excerpts: 

- Product: Very strong signal on understanding customer pain; tied trade-offs to measurable metrics (latency budget, cost per request).
- System design: Good high-level decomposition but when pressed on cross-region failover they deferred to "we'd use db replicas" without specifying failover detection, reconciliation windows, or API semantics. That matters for our multi-region SLAs.
- Communication/Ownership: Ran the debrief well, volunteered past incidents and owned a postmortem example.

My vote: Yes (conditional) — I will mark a "Yes — needs system design onboarding plan" in the scorecard. If the hiring manager is comfortable with a short remediation plan (2–4 week onboarding goals around cross-region failover), I'm happy to push.

If you want to sync I can do 3:00–3:20pm PDT.

--
Marissa Cole
Staff PM, Platform

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priya Shah — rapid clarity sprint & evidence log

Appreciate the quick uploads and the flagged risk. Two operational asks as I'm consolidating for the hiring manager: 

1) Please paste one short "signal line" per rubric area into the Notion page (just 1 sentence or a direct quote). It makes the packet readable.
2) Vote: "Yes", "Yes (with plan)", or "No" — one word in reply.

Rubric anchoring guidance (use these as a guide when you write the signal line):
- "Yes" anchor: Candidate demonstrates independent shipping history + 3+ concrete trade-off examples and < 2 major architectural gaps.
- "Yes (with plan)" anchor: Strong product/ownership/communication but a focused technical gap that can be closed in ramp (we want explicit onboarding milestones).
- "No" anchor: Multiple architectural misunderstandings or behavioral concerns.

If we hit split votes, I'll schedule a 20m panel sync at 4:00pm PDT. I can also act as the tiebreak if needed.

Grace

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Priya Shah — rapid clarity sprint & evidence log

Yes (with plan).

Signal lines I added to Notion: 
- Product: "Connected trade-offs to impact; prioritized latency for first 90 days with measurable metric plan."
- System design: "Sound decomposition but missed explicit failover detection and reconciliation windows — recommend onboarding milestone to close this."
- Code craft: "Discussed bounded-priority queue and complexity — solid mental model."
- Communication: "Clear, concise, handled ambiguities well and owned a past incident."

Short summary for hiring manager: Strong product and ownership; system-design gap is fixable with two onboarding goals (failover detection design + cross-region reconciliation plan). Recommend extend an offer contingent on an initial 30-day technical onboarding plan.

Tessa
